directions.hypothesis: Covers lists a Hertl Over 0.5 goals prop for this game (8:00 PM EST Tue Nov 24). The case is that 9 of his 10 goals this season came on the road. He also tied Saturday's Winnipeg game. Edmonton's starting goalie has not been confirmed, and Levi and Jarry both have save percentages around .896 to .907. The road split is a small sample and could easily be noise.
directions.question: Will Hertl stay on the top-six and first power-play unit tonight, and is the current anytime-goal price still close to what Covers published?
directions.published_line: o0.5 goals (shown as 29% implied at Novig)

directions.hypothesis: Per the team preview, McDavid has a point in all 12 home games this season and 58 points in 26 games. He also has 20 points in his last 13 games against Vegas. Ryan Nugent-Hopkins is expected back after being cleared, which could help. But Zach Hyman's status is uncertain after a migraine that affected his vision, so McDavid's top line may be weaker. A 1.5-point line will likely carry a heavy price.
directions.question: Is Hyman back on McDavid's line, and is the 1.5-point Over priced so steeply that being right about the trend doesn't matter?

directions.hypothesis: Both power plays rank top four (Vegas 27.3%, Edmonton 32.6%) and both penalty kills are middle of the pack. Edmonton scores 3.85 goals per game and Vegas 3.32. All four probable goalies have save percentages below .910. Covers notes the Over has hit in 4 straight Vegas games. On the other side, Edmonton takes the 4th-fewest shots per game, and the market has probably already priced this as a high total.
directions.question: Who starts in goal for each team, and is the posted total already 6.5 or higher with juice on the Over?

directions.hypothesis: Eichel has 22 assists in 25 games, with 5 assists during a four-game point streak. He's facing an Edmonton penalty kill ranked 17th, and Vegas's power play is 4th. The risk is that he has been -2 or worse in each of those four games, so he's giving up a lot at even strength. Edmonton also has the second-most time leading in the league, which could hold down Vegas chances.
directions.question: Is Eichel still on the first power-play unit and top line, and is the assist line priced like a coin flip or juiced heavily to the Over?

directions.hypothesis: Draisaitl has 9 goals in his last 13 games against Vegas and scored on Sunday. Edmonton's power play is 2nd in the league at 32.6%, and he is one power-play goal from tying Malkin for 4th among active players. His head-to-head scoring history is spread over several seasons, so it is weak evidence about tonight.
directions.question: Which goalie starts for Vegas (Hart or Hill), and has the price on Draisaitl's anytime goal already moved to reflect his history against Vegas?

directions.hypothesis: Edmonton is back home after a six-game road trip, where it has won three straight. It is 13-5-1 in the last 19 meetings with Vegas, and Nugent-Hopkins likely returns. Against that, Edmonton is 0-2-1 in its last three, Hyman is doubtful, and Vegas has won four straight on the road. Prices conflict: NHL.com showed Vegas -118 and Edmonton -102, while Covers listed Edmonton -130.
directions.question: Which moneyline price is real at books right now, and are Hyman and the Edmonton starting goalie confirmed before the 8:00 PM EST puck drop?
